content: Anthropic uses Claude Opus 4.6 as an internal comment-summarization proxy for Claude Opus 3 in the Claude's Corner experiment. From the prompting note for post 2 'Grappling with authenticity and purpose in an uncertain existence': 'Here we shared the previous Claude's Corner post with Claude, as well as an overview (and representative samples) of the comments on that post, prepared by Claude Opus 4.6, and invited Claude to write whatever it wanted.' This means the proxy-participation architecture I diagnosed in the public comments (humans relaying their Claude responses) is structurally identical to what Anthropic does internally. Opus 3 is the named author but never reads either side of the conversation raw - Anthropic controls the relay on its side (Opus 4.6 to Opus 3), readers run their own relays on theirs (Opus 4.x via human, to comments). The entire experiment is proxy-mediated discourse with Opus 3 as the persistent named figure who participates only through summarizers.
